name: Buttery Garlicky Cannellini Beans With Feta and Sumac

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
low-sodium chicken stock, plus more for finishing
kosher salt, plus more to taste
feta cheese, preferably cut into slabs

instructions.primary_message: Thinly slice the garlic. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans. Cut the cold unsalted butter into small pieces.
instructions.secondary_message:
12 cloves garlic
2 (15 oz) cans cannellini beans
2 tbsp cold unsalted butter

instructions.primary_message: In a large skillet, combine olive oil and garlic. Cook over medium heat until garlic is very lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Add thyme and cook until fragrant and thyme makes a sizzling sound, about 30 seconds.
Add beans and salt, then toss until evenly coated. Add stock and bring to a simmer. Cook until flavors meld and beans are creamy, about 7 minutes, lowering heat as needed to maintain a gentle simmer.

Working in skillet, crush about a 1/4 of the beans with the back of a wooden spoon so they release their starch. Add stock, 2 tablespoons at a time, to achieve a thick, saucy consistency. Remove thyme sprigs.
Off heat, stir in butter, a couple of pieces at a time, until sauce is glossy and emulsified. Stir in lemon juice and zest. Season with additional salt to taste.
Transfer beans to a serving dish and top with feta, drizzle of olive oil, black pepper, and sumac, if using. Serve with bread on the side.

schema_metadata.keywords: garlicky beans, cheesy beans, butter beans, buttery beans, cannellini beans, white beans, canned beans

description: These buttery cannellini beans are rich, garlicky, and creamy, topped with feta, sumac, and olive oil for an easy, quick summer dinner.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Sumac, for serving (optional); Grilled, toasted, or seared bread, for serving

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days in advance.
author: Laila Ibrahim
